{{WotQ|{{PAGENAME}}}}
{{dablink|For the expansion of ''The Wheel of Time Roleplaying Game'' by the same name, see ''[[The Wheel of Time Roleplaying Game#The Prophecies of the Dragon|The Prophecies of the Dragon]].'' For other uses of the word "dragon," see [[Dragon (disambiguation)|Dragon]].}}
The '''''Karaethon Cycle''''' contains the ''Prophecies of the Dragon'', which are believed to detail <!--the secrets of  ???--> how the [[Dragon]] will be [[Reborn]] and what his coming will mean for both the [[Light]] and the [[Shadow]]. They consist of a collection of [[Foretelling]]s from before{{verify}}, during, and after the [[War of Power]].  Many are vague and can only be understood in hindsight.  Most people avoid them, and they are banned in many lands. 

{{quote|The Karaethon Cycle, – Thom said curtly.
Rand blinked. The Prophecies of the Dragon.  – Nobody tells the ... those stories in the Two Rivers. Not in Emond's Field, anyway. The Wisdom would skin them alive, if they did. {{ref/book|1|13}}}}

{{quote| Telling the Prophecies of the Dragon, or even possessing a copy of them, is enough to put you in prison, in Tear. {{ref/book|3|6}}}}

== The Karaethon Cycle: The Prophecies of the Dragon ==
And it shall come to pass that what men made shall be shattered,<br />
and the [[Shadow]] shall lie across the [[Pattern#The Pattern|Pattern]] of the Age,<br />
and the [[Dark One]] shall once more lay his hand upon the world of man.<br />
Women shall weep and men quail as the nations of the earth are rent like rotting cloth.<br />
Neither shall anything stand or abide...

The Shadow shall rise across the world, and darken every land, even to the smallest corner, and there shall be neither Light nor safety.<br />
And he who shall be born of the Dawn{{ref|Rand and Mat return to Chaendaer where they are met by the Bair. Couladin claims Rand murdered Muradin and attacks him. Before any damage is done, Bair stops them and has Rand show the signs. Couladin and the Shaido stand on one side. Rhuarc, Heirn and the Jindo stand on another. Lan stands in between. Egwene, Amys, Melaine and Seana come out of the tents. They all see that Rand has dragons on both arms. Bair announces that a Car'a'carn, "chief of chiefs" in the Old Tongue, has been chosen.}}{{ref/book|4|34}}, born of the [[Shaiel|Maiden]], according to [[Prophecy of Rhuidean|Prophecy]], <br />
he shall stretch forth his hands to catch the Shadow,<br />
and the world shall scream in the pain of salvation.<br />
All Glory be to the Creator, and to the Light, and to he who shall be born again. May the Light save us from him.<br />

Yet [[Dragon Reborn|one]] shall be born to face the Shadow,<br />
born once more as [[Lews Therin Telamon|he]] was born before,<br />
and shall be born again, time without end.<br />
The [[Dragon]] shall be Reborn,<br />
and there will be wailing and gnashing of teeth at his rebirth.<br />
In sackcloth and ashes shall he clothe the people,<br />
and he shall break the world again by his coming,<br />
tearing apart all ties that bind.<br />
Like the unfettered dawn shall he blind us, and burn us,<br />
yet shall the Dragon Reborn confront the Shadow at the [[Last Battle]],<br />
and his blood shall give us the Light.<br />
Let tears flow, O ye people of the world.<br />
Weep for your salvation.{{Ref/book|2|prologue}}

On the slopes of [[Dragonmount]] shall he be born,{{ref|[[Tam]] hints that he found a babe cold in the snow and that his wife named the child Rand during a fever dream after Trollocs attacked his farm.}}{{ref/book|1|6}}<br />
born of a [[Maiden of the Spear|maiden]] wedded to no man. {{ref|Elayne recalls a line from the Prophecies of the Dragon, "On the slopes of Dragonmount shall he be born, born of a maiden wedded to no man." She notes that Rand looks like an Aiel and also looks like Tigraine as well. Egwene recalls what Moiraine told her about Tam and Kari al'Thor not being Rand's real parents.}}{{ref/book|3|39}}{{ref|[[Rand al'Thor]]'s mother was [[Tigraine Mantear]], who left her life as [[Daughter-Heir]] of [[Andor]], under the direction of [[Gitara Sedai]], to become a [[Far Dareis Mai|Maiden of the Spear]]. His father was [[Janduin]], a clan chief.}}{{ref/book|4|34}}.<br />
He will be of the [[Aiel|ancient blood]], and raised by the [[Manetheren|old blood]].{{ref|The ancient blood references Rand al'Thor's Aiel ancestry; the old blood refers to him being raised [[Tam al'Thor]], a descendant of [[Manetheren]].}}{{ref/book|2|8}}<br />
When the winds of [[Tarmon Gai'don]] scour the earth,<br />
he will face the Shadow and bring forth Light again in the world.{{ref|{{Amol}}}}<br />
For he shall come like the breaking dawn,<br />
and shatter the world again with his coming, and make it anew.{{ref|As quoted by [[Siuan Sanche]].}}{{ref/book|2|5}}

[[Rand al'Thor#Appearance|Twice and twice shall he be marked]]{{ref|As quoted by [[Thomdril Merrilin]].}}{{ref/book|2|26}},<br />
twice to live, and twice to die.<br />
Once the heron, to set his path.{{ref|[[Ishamael]] attacks [[Rand]] in his dreams with fire as the Dragon holds [[Tam's Sword]]. The fire sears a heron on Rand's hand when he awakens.}}{{ref/book|2|15}}<br />
Twice the heron, to name him true.{{ref|[[Rand]] and [[Ishamael]] fight in the sky at [[Falme]]. Rand uses the [[Oneness]] and ''[[saidin]]'' to make him one with [[Tam al'Thor's sword|Tam's sword]].{{2|47}} After his victory, the fight leaves another heron seared into the other hand.{{2|49}}}}<br />
Once the Dragon, for remembrance lost.{{ref|''Remembrance lost'' is the history of the [[Aiel]], shown through the [[Glass columns]] in [[Rhuidean]].}}{{ref/book|4|25}}{{ref/book|4|26}}<br />
Twice the Dragon, for the price he must pay.{{ref|{{Amol}}}}

Five ride forth,{{ref|[[Perrin]], [[Rand]], [[Mat]], [[Hurin]], and [[Ingtar]] are the first to volunteer to enter [[Falme]]. Verin does not allow anyone else to go.}}{{ref/book|2|44}} and four return.{{ref|[[Ingtar]] refuses to leave with the group and confesses his sins to Rand with hopes that his sacrifice will lead to repentance.}}{{ref/book|2|46}}<br />
Above [[the Watchers Over the Waves]] shall he proclaim himself,<br />
bannered 'cross the sky in fire.{{ref|[[Rand]] and [[Ishamael]] fight in the sky at [[Falme]].}}{{ref/book|2|47}}

The [[Stone of Tear]] will never fall, till [[Callandor]] is wielded by the Dragon’s hand.{{ref|[[Rand]] infiltrates the Stone at takes ''Callandor'' out of desperation. The Stone does not fall until after he proclaims himself.}}{{ref/book|3|55}}<br />
The Stone of Tear will never fall, till the [[People of the Dragon]] come.{{ref|As quoted by [[Thomdril Merrilin]].}}{{ref/book|1|13}}{{ref|The [[Aiel]] infiltrate Tear and sneak into the Stone prior to Rand's third fight with Ishamael.}}{{ref/book|3|54}}

Into the heart he thrusts his sword,{{ref|Rand thrusts ''[[Callandor]]'' into the [[Heart of the Stone]] within the [[Stone of Tear]], telling the [[Tairen]]s that he will come back for the sword.}}{{ref/book|4|21}}<br />
into the heart, to hold their hearts.{{ref|Rand admits to Moiraine that he left ''Callandor'' in Tear in order to bind the Tairens to him because they will fear his return.}}{{ref/book|5|2}}<br />
[[Jahar Narishma|who draws it out]] shall follow after,{{ref|[[Jahar Narishma]] draws the sword out for Rand prior to his Altaran Campaign against the [[Seanchan]].}}{{ref/book|5|21}}<br />
What hand can grasp that [[Callandor|fearful blade]]?

Power of the Shadow made human flesh{{ref|The first [[Bubble of evil]] Rand experiences turns his reflections into human flesh.}}{{ref/book|4|2}}<br />
[[Bubbles of evil|wakened to turmoil, strife and ruin.]]<br />
The Reborn One, marked and bleeding,{{ref|This is Rand after his travels through the [[Glass columns]] and is marked as the ''[[Car'a'carn]]''.}}{{ref/book|4|26}}<br />
dances the sword in dreams and mist,{{ref|Rand and Mat flee the mist covered [[Rhuidean]] when a [[Bubble of evil]] creates creatures out of sand.}}{{ref/book|4|26}}<br />
chains the [[Forsaken|Shadowsworn]] to his will,{{ref|Rand defeats [[Asmodean]] by severing his connection to the [[Dark One]], leaving him no choice but to help Rand or risk execution from the other [[Forsaken]].}}{{ref/book|4|58}}<br />
from the city, lost and forsaken,{{ref|Rand defeats [[Asmodean]] in [[Rhuidean]].}}{{ref/book|4|24}}<br />
leads the [[Siswai'aman|spears]] to war once more,{{ref|[[Moiraine]] asks [[Rand]] where will he ''lead the spears to war once more'' in [[Cold Rocks Hold]] once she understands that the ''spears'' in prophecy point to the [[Aiel]], not the [[Tairen]]s.}}{{ref/book|4|49}}{{ref|When Moiraine prods Rand, he admits that his plan to lead all eleven [[Clan]]s across the [[Dragonwall]] in order to quell the nations through strength, not diplomacy as Moiraine planned.}}{{ref/book|5|2}}{{ref|When news of [[Shaido]] and their departure from the [[Aiel Waste]] reaches [[Rand]], he orders the [[Clan chief]]s to rouse the spears and follow him.}}{{ref/book|5|7}}<br />
breaks the spears and makes them see,{{ref|Rand tells the [[Aiel]] at [[Alcair Dal]] about a time when they followed the [[Way of the Leaf]], creating the [[Bleakness]].}}{{ref/book|4|57}}<br />
truth long hidden in the ancient dream.{{ref|The Aiel history hidden in the [[Glass columns]] in [[Rhuidean]].}}{{ref/book|4|25}}{{ref/book|4|26}}

He shall slay [[Aiel|his people]] with the sword of peace, and destroy them with the [[Way of the Leaf|leaf]].{{ref|As quoted by [[Moiraine]].|Moiraine}}{{ref/book|3|6}}{{ref|Rand tells the [[Aiel]] at [[Alcair Dal]] about a time when they followed the [[Way of the Leaf]], creating the [[Bleakness]].}}{{ref/book|4|57}}

With his coming are the dread fires born again.<br />
The hills burn, and the land turns sere.<br />
The tides of men run out, and the hours dwindle.<br />
The wall is pierced, and the veil of parting raised.<br />
Storms rumble beyond the horizon, and the fires of heaven purge the earth.<br />
There is no salvation without destruction, no hope this side of death.{{ref|Fragment from The [[Prophecies of the Dragon]] believed translated by [[N'Delia Basolaine]], [[First Maid]] and Swordfast to [[Raidhen]] of [[Hol Cuchone]] (circa {{ab|400}}).}}{{ref/book|5|prologue}}

[[White Tower|The unstained tower]], broken, bends knee to the forgotten sign.{{ref|After the battle of [[Dumai's Wells]], Rand counts twenty-three [[Aes Sedai]] prisoners from the [[White Tower]]...and nine representatives from the [[Salidar Aes Sedai]] Because they brought nine when he said six, he now places them on the same level at the other Aes Sedai and orders them to kneel. With the ''forgotten sign'', the ancient [[Aes Sedai symbol]] above everyone, the ''unstained tower, broken'' represented by the two groups of Aes Sedai, swear fealty to the Dragon Reborn.}}{{ref/book|6|55}}<br />
The seas rage, and stormclouds gather unseen.<br />
Beyond the horizon, hidden fires swell, and serpents nestle in the bosom.<br />
What was exalted is cast down; what was cast down is raised up.<br />
Order burns to clear his path.{{ref|The [[Prophecies of the Dragon]] translation by [[Jeorad Manyard]] Governor of the Province of [[Andor]] for the High King, [[Artur Paendrag Tanreall]].}}{{ref/book|6|epilogue}}

There can be no health in us, nor any good thing grow,<br />
for the land is one with the Dragon Reborn, and he is one with the land.<br />
Soul of fire, heart of stone, in pride he conquers, forcing the proud to yield.<br />
He calls upon the mountains to kneel, and the seas to give way, and the very skies to bow.<br />
Pray that the heart of stone remembers tears, and the soul of fire, love.{{ref|From a much-disputed translation by the poet Kyera Termendal of [[Shiota]], believed to have been published between {{fy|700}} and {{fy|800}}.}}{{ref/book|7|prologue}}

As the plow breaks the earth shall he break the lives of men,<br />
and all that was shall be consumed in the fire of his eyes.<br />
The trumpets of war shall sound at his footsteps, the ravens feed at his voice,<br />
and he shall wear a crown of swords.{{ref/book|7|18}}

Master of the lightnings, rider on the storm,<br />
wearer of a [[Crown of Swords|crown of swords]], spinner out of fate.<br />
Who thinks he turns the Wheel of Time,<br />
may learn the truth too late.{{ref|{{7|41}} - From a fragmentary translation attributed to Lord [[Mangore Kiramin]],
Sword-bard of [[Aramaelle]] and [[Warder]] to [[Caraighan Maconar]], into what was then called the vulgar tongue, circa {{ab|300}}.}}

[[Seven Seals|The Seals]] that hold back the night shall weaken,<br />
and in the heart of winter shall winter’s heart be born,<br />
amid the wailings of lamentation and the gnashing of teeth,<br />
for winter’s heart shall ride a black horse, and the name of it is [[Moridin|Death]]. {{ref/book|9|Prologue}}

And it shall come to pass, in the days when the Dark Hunt rides,<br />
when the right hand falters and the left hand strays,<br />
that mankind shall come to the Crossroads of Twilight,<br />
and all that is, all that was,<br />
and all that will be shall balance on the point of a sword,<br />
while the winds of the Shadow grow.{{ref|{{10|prologue}} - From the translation believed done by [[Jain Charin]], known as Jain Farstrider, shortly before his disappearance.}}

[[Cleansing of saidin|He shall heal the wounds of madness]] and cutting of hope.{{ref||Moiraine}}

He shall hold a [[Callandor|blade of light]] in his hands, and the three shall be one.{{ref/book|12|45}}

He shall bind [[Court of the Nine Moons|the nine moons]] to serve him.{{ref||Moiraine}}
The north shall he tie to the east, and the west shall be bound to the south. {{ref/book|7|34}}

Twice dawns the day when his blood is shed.<ref>In AMoL it is referenced that the third age ends and the fourth age began at noon referencing a death and birth during the final battle.</ref><br />
Once for mourning, once for birth.<br />
Red on black, the Dragon’s blood stains the rock of [[Shayol Ghul]].<br />
In the [[Pit of Doom]] shall his blood free men from the Shadow. {{ref/book|2|26}}

His blood on the rocks of Shayol Ghul,<br />
washing away the Shadow, sacrifice for man’s salvation. {{ref/book|4|3}}

He shall break chains and put others into chains.{{ref||Moiraine}}

Fortune rides like the sun on high{{ref|Fortune rides like the sun on high" - This can be literal, given that Tuon's name is Fortuona and she literally rode with the Fox (Mat). On the other hand, metaphorically, the phrase "rides like the sun on high" may also be a reference to Fortuona as Empress of the Seanchan. Or this could be a reference to Mat's specific brand of ''[[ta'veren]]'' nature, dealing in especially good, or bad, luck and fortune.}}<br />
with the fox that makes the ravens fly.<br />
Luck his soul, the lightning his eye,<br />
He snatches the moons from out of the sky.{{ref/book|10|28}}

When the Wolf King carries the hammer, thus are the final days known.<br />
When the Fox marries the raven, and the trumpets of battle are blown. {{ref/book|11|4}}

== Commentaries ==
Several books have been written about the Karaethon Cycle and the Prophecies of the Dragon.
[[Commentary on the Dragon]], by [[Sajius]] is one such book.

Some of these works may have been written in the style of prophecy themselves, with the authors incorporating their interpretations into the translations.

{{WotQ|Commentaries on the Karaethon Cycle}}
{{WotQ|Commentaries on the Prophecies of the Dragon}}

== Statements about the Prophecies ==
These are statements describing the contents of the prophecies, not quoting them.

"When the Dragon is Reborn he will break all oaths, shatter all ties."{{ref|{{2|46}} - Paraphrased by [[Uno Nomesta]]}}

"And prophecy said the [[Horn of Valere]] would only be found just in time for the Last Battle."{{ref|{{2|5}} - Paraphrased by [[Siuan Sanche]]}}

The Karaethon Cycle does not mention the Horn of Valere, except that it must be found before the [[Last Battle]]. {{ref/book|2|20}}
